Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a well-defined, rounded opacity in the right mid-lung zone (right middle lobe) with somewhat ill-defined or spiculated margins, which is a classic radiographic presentation for primary lung cancer (such as adenocarcinoma). While round pneumonia can present similarly, it is less common in adults and typically has smoother margins; metastatic disease usually presents with multiple nodules rather than a solitary mass.
